claim: Down syndrome (DS) is caused by trisomy 21 and is the most common survivable aneuploidy, occurring in about 1 in every 800 live births.
source: Down syndrome (DS) is caused by trisomy 21 and is the most common survivable aneuploidy, occurring in about 1 in every 800 in live births (Driscoll and Gross, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Driscoll and Gross, 2009

claim: People with DS have intellectual disabilities, a high risk of congenital heart disease and leukemia, and early onset dementia.
source: Besides common facial and other physical features, people with DS have intellectual disabilities, a high risk of congenital heart disease and leukemia, and early onset dementia (Korenberg et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citation to Korenberg et al., 1994

claim: 95% of DS cases have a complete freely segregating third copy of HSA21.
source: A population-based study of 6300 infants with DS born from 1993 to 2003 in US shows that 95% had a complete freely segregating third copy of HSA21, 3% had partial trisomy 21 due to duplication of part of the chromosome, and 2% had mosaic DS in which some cells have three copies of HSA21 while others have two copies (Shin et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shin et al., 2010, a population-based study

claim: 3% of DS cases have partial trisomy 21 due to duplication of part of the chromosome.
source: A population-based study of 6300 infants with DS born from 1993 to 2003 in US shows that 95% had a complete freely segregating third copy of HSA21, 3% had partial trisomy 21 due to duplication of part of the chromosome, and 2% had mosaic DS in which some cells have three copies of HSA21 while others have two copies (Shin et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shin et al., 2010, a population-based study

claim: 2% of DS cases have mosaic DS in which some cells have three copies of HSA21 while others have two copies.
source: A population-based study of 6300 infants with DS born from 1993 to 2003 in US shows that 95% had a complete freely segregating third copy of HSA21, 3% had partial trisomy 21 due to duplication of part of the chromosome, and 2% had mosaic DS in which some cells have three copies of HSA21 while others have two copies (Shin et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shin et al., 2010, a population-based study

claim: Both translocation DS and mosaic DS are rare and typically have milder phenotypes compared with those who inherit a complete HSA21.
source: Both translocation DS and mosaic DS are rare and typically have milder phenotypes compared with those who inherit a complete HSA21 (Prasher, 1995; Chandra et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Prasher, 1995 and Chandra et al., 2010

claim: Ts65Dn was the first viable DS mouse model.
source: Davisson's Ts65Dn mouse was the first viable DS model (Davisson et al., 1990; Davisson et al., 1993), and the demonstration that features directly comparable to those in DS occurred in mice with trisomy for a number of genes orthologous to HSA21 changed the paradigm for research in this area (Reeves et al., 1995).
evidence: Supported by citations to Davisson et al., 1990 and 1993

claim: Features directly comparable to those in DS occurred in mice with trisomy for a number of genes orthologous to HSA21.
source: Davisson's Ts65Dn mouse was the first viable DS model (Davisson et al., 1990; Davisson et al., 1993), and the demonstration that features directly comparable to those in DS occurred in mice with trisomy for a number of genes orthologous to HSA21 changed the paradigm for research in this area (Reeves et al., 1995).
evidence: Supported by citation to Reeves et al., 1995

claim: Ts65Dn has been the most broadly used model for DS research for more than two decades.
source: Ts65Dn has been the most broadly used model for DS research for more than two decades, up to and including crucial support for clinical trials (Braudeau et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Braudeau et al., 2011

claim: More than a dozen pharmaceuticals or nutriceuticals have reported promising effects in Ts65Dn mice.
source: Testing of potential treatments in Ts65Dn mice has yielded an embarrassment of riches with more than a dozen pharmaceuticals or nutriceuticals reporting promising effects (Fernandez and Reeves, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fernandez and Reeves, 2015

claim: The Roche clinical trial of the GABA-α5 antagonist RG1662 was terminated in Phase IIa due to lack of efficacy in a long term treatment paradigm.
source: Improvements with RG1662 are dramatic in mice, but the human trial was terminated in Phase IIa due to lack of efficacy in a long term treatment paradigm (https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT02024789).
evidence: Supported by reference to clinical trial registry

claim: The current machine-based annotation of HSA21 shows that there are 17 and 213 protein coding genes (PCGs) mapped to the short (HSA21p) and long arms of HSA21 (HSA21q), respectively.
source: The current machine-based annotation of HSA21 (GRCh38.p12, BioMart-Ensembl, May 2019) shows that there are 17 and 213 protein coding genes (PCGs) mapped to the short (HSA21p) and long arms of HSA21 (HSA21q), respectively.
evidence: Based on specific genome annotation database (GRCh38.p12, BioMart-Ensembl, May 2019)

claim: 15 of 17 HSA21p PCGs are identified by BLASTN as base-perfect copies/duplications of HSA21q.
source: However, 15 of 17 HSA21p PCGs are identified by BLASTN as base-perfect copies/duplications of HSA21q, and BAGE2 and TPTE are the only unique HSA21 PCGs in HSA21p (Table 1).
evidence: Supported by BLASTN analysis and Table 1

claim: BAGE2 and TPTE are the only unique HSA21 PCGs in HSA21p.
source: However, 15 of 17 HSA21p PCGs are identified by BLASTN as base-perfect copies/duplications of HSA21q, and BAGE2 and TPTE are the only unique HSA21 PCGs in HSA21p (Table 1).
evidence: Supported by BLASTN analysis and Table 1

claim: Tc1 is the only existing DS mouse model carrying HSA21.
source: A transchromosomic (Tc) HSA21 mouse line, Tc1, is the only existing DS mouse model carrying HSA21.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge of existing DS mouse models

claim: The HSA21 in Tc1 was irradiated in the process of creating Tc1 mice, and more than 50 PCGs on HSA21q are disrupted by rearrangement, deletion or duplication.
source: The HSA21 was irradiated in the process of creating Tc1 mice, and more than 50 PCGs on HSA21q are disrupted by rearrangement, deletion or duplication (Gribble et al., 2013; O'Doherty et al., 2005; Choong et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gribble et al., 2013; O'Doherty et al., 2005; Choong et al., 2015

claim: Tc1 includes 158 of 213 functionally trisomic HSA21q PCGs.
source: Tc1 thus includes 158 of 213 functionally trisomic HSA21q PCGs (Table 1—source data 1B).
evidence: Supported by data in Table 1—source data 1B

claim: All Tc1 mice are mosaic for HSA21.
source: An important limitation of Tc1 is that all mice are mosaic for HSA21.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about Tc1 mice

claim: Mosaicism makes each Tc1 mouse unique from every other mouse, because the developmental trajectories dependent on cell-cell interactions are different in every individual.
source: Mosaicism makes each Tc1 mouse unique from every other mouse, because the developmental trajectories dependent on cell-cell interactions are different in every individual (Besson, 2005; Roper and Reeves, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Besson, 2005 and Roper and Reeves, 2006

claim: The retention rates of human chromosomes and human artificial chromosomes (HACs) vary widely in different mouse tissues.
source: Mosaicism in Tc1 is not an isolated case, as the retention rates of other human chromosomes and human artificial chromosomes (HACs) vary widely in different mouse tissues (Shinohara et al., 2000; Tomizuka et al., 1997; Takiguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Shinohara et al., 2000; Tomizuka et al., 1997; Takiguchi et al., 2014

claim: The centromere is a multi-function regulator of genome stability and linked to chromosomal instability found in the interspecific hybrids.
source: The centromere is a multi-function regulator of genome stability and linked to chromosomal instability found in the interspecific hybrids (Lerit and Poulton, 2016; Metcalfe et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lerit and Poulton, 2016 and Metcalfe et al., 2007

claim: TcMAC21 contains a nearly complete and freely segregating HSA21q as a mouse artificial chromosome.
source: TcMAC21 contains a nearly complete and freely segregating HSA21q as a mouse artificial chromosome and has no detectable mosaicism in a broad spectrum of tissues and cell types.
evidence: Based on the experimental results described in the manuscript

claim: TcMAC21 has no detectable mosaicism in a broad spectrum of tissues and cell types.
source: TcMAC21 contains a nearly complete and freely segregating HSA21q as a mouse artificial chromosome and has no detectable mosaicism in a broad spectrum of tissues and cell types.
evidence: Based on the experimental results described in the manuscript

claim: TcMAC21 is the most complete genetic model of DS created to date with 93% of HSA21q PCGs and about 79% of non-PCGs present.
source: It is the most complete genetic model of DS created to date with 93% of HSA21q PCGs and about 79% of non-PCGs present.
evidence: Based on the WGS and annotation data presented in the manuscript

claim: The MAC1 vector contains the centromeric region of MMU11.
source: The MAC1 vector contains the centromeric region of MMU11 (Takiguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Takiguchi et al., 2014

claim: A loxP site was introduced into the NC_000021.9 locus (from 13,021,348 bp to 13,028,858 bp) of HSA21 to create the 'HSA21-loxP' chromosome.
source: A loxP site was introduced into the NC_000021.9 locus (from 13,021,348 bp to 13,028,858 bp) of HSA21 to create the 'HSA21-loxP' chromosome, which was transferred by MMCT into Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells containing the MAC1 vector (Figure 1A).
evidence: Described in methods and shown in Figure 1A

claim: Reciprocal translocation between the MAC1 vector and HSA21-loxP was induced by a transient Cre expression to produce the target hybrid chromosome, 'HSA21q-MAC'.
source: Reciprocal translocation between the MAC1 vector and HSA21-loxP was induced by a transient Cre expression to produce the target hybrid chromosome, 'HSA21q-MAC', containing the centromere plus 2.5 kb of the peri-centromeric region of MMU11 (without producing any transcripts) and HSA21q (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Described in methods and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: The HSA21q-MAC contains the centromere plus 2.5 kb of the peri-centromeric region of MMU11 (without producing any transcripts) and HSA21q.
source: Reciprocal translocation between the MAC1 vector and HSA21-loxP was induced by a transient Cre expression to produce the target hybrid chromosome, 'HSA21q-MAC', containing the centromere plus 2.5 kb of the peri-centromeric region of MMU11 (without producing any transcripts) and HSA21q (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Described in methods and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: 16 out of the 18 drug-resistant clones were PCR-positive with Cre-loxP recombination-specific primers.
source: The recombinant clones were selected using HAT, and 16 out of the 18 drug-resistant clones were PCR-positive with Cre-loxP recombination-specific primers.
evidence: Based on experimental data from the recombination process

claim: Two lines out of the examined eight clones were confirmed by FISH to contain HSA21q-MAC.
source: Two lines out of the examined eight clones were confirmed by FISH to contain HSA21q-MAC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: Based on FISH data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C

claim: WGS confirmed that the HSA21q in TcMAC21 extends from the loxP site at base pair 13,021,348 to the telomere at 46,691,226.
source: WGS confirmed that the HSA21q in TcMAC21 extends from the loxP site at base pair 13,021,348 to the telomere at 46,691,226.
evidence: Based on whole genome sequencing data

claim: The HSA21q in TcMAC21 contains all annotated HSA21q PCGs from POTED to PRMT2 and all except one non-PCG, AP001464.1.
source: This region contains all annotated HSA21q PCGs from POTED to PRMT2 and all except one non-PCG, AP001464.1.
evidence: Based on whole genome sequencing data

claim: WGS revealed four deletions in the transchromosome.
source: WGS revealed four deletions in the transchromosome (Figure 1E).
evidence: Based on whole genome sequencing data shown in Figure 1E

claim: Physical deletions encompassed ~29% of HSA21q, but they occurred substantially in PCG-poor regions, and only 14 of 213 HSA21q PCGs were deleted.
source: While physical deletions encompassed ~29% of HSA21q, they occurred substantially in PCG-poor regions, and only 14 of 213 HSA21q PCGs were deleted (Figure 1F and Figure 1—source data 1B–C).
evidence: Based on whole genome sequencing data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—source data 1B–C

claim: There were 91 single nucleotide variations (SNVs) in HSA21q identified by WGS, and 90 of 91 were previously reported as native alternative alleles.
source: There were 91 single nucleotide variations (SNVs) in HSA21q identified by WGS, and we confirmed that 90 of 91 were previously reported as native alternative alleles (Figure 1—source data 1D).
evidence: Based on whole genome sequencing data shown in Figure 1—source data 1D

claim: A new SNV was observed in the SON gene (HSA21: 33,554,276 (reference (C) and SNV(A), P1682Q).
source: A new SNV was observed in the SON gene (HSA21: 33,554,276 (reference (C) and SNV(A), P1682Q).
evidence: Based on whole genome sequencing data

claim: Annotation with SIFT predicts that the SON SNV is likely to be tolerated.
source: Annotation with SIFT predicts that the SON SNV is likely to be tolerated, and RNA-Seq (below) demonstrates the presence of a human SON mRNA.
evidence: Based on SIFT prediction tool analysis

claim: RNA-Seq demonstrates the presence of a human SON mRNA.
source: Annotation with SIFT predicts that the SON SNV is likely to be tolerated, and RNA-Seq (below) demonstrates the presence of a human SON mRNA.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data

claim: Neither 49 HSA21q keratin associated protein genes (KRTAPs) nor their mouse orthologs were expressed in TcMAC21 or Eu brain.
source: Neither 49 HSA21q keratin associated protein genes (KRTAPs) nor their mouse orthologs were expressed in TcMAC21 or Eu brain.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data from P1 forebrain

claim: In TcMAC21, 66.5% of HSA21 PCGs and 11.1% of HSA21 non-PCGs had medium or high expression (measured as FPKM >0.5).
source: In TcMAC21, 66.5% of HSA21 PCGs and 11.1% of HSA21 non-PCGs had medium or high expression (measured as fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped reads (FPKM) >0.5), and 36.5% of HSA21 PCGs and 1.2% of HSA21 non-PCGs had high expression (FPKM >5) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1A).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1A

claim: In TcMAC21, 36.5% of HSA21 PCGs and 1.2% of HSA21 non-PCGs had high expression (FPKM >5).
source: In TcMAC21, 66.5% of HSA21 PCGs and 11.1% of HSA21 non-PCGs had medium or high expression (measured as fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped reads (FPKM) >0.5), and 36.5% of HSA21 PCGs and 1.2% of HSA21 non-PCGs had high expression (FPKM >5) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1A).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1A

claim: The most proximal HSA21q non-PCG and PCG, ANKRD30BP2 (FPKM = 5.3) and POTED (FPKM = 2.4), respectively, were detected as expressed.
source: The most proximal HSA21q non-PCG and PCG, ANKRD30BP2 (13,038,159–13,067,033, FPKM = 5.3) and POTED (13,038,159–13,067,033, FPKM = 2.4), respectively, were detected as expressed, as were the most distal HSA21q non-PCG and PCG, DSTNP1 (46,635,166–46,665,124, FPKM = 6.5) and PRMT2 (46,635,166–46,665,124, FPKM = 60.2) (Figure 2B).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2B

claim: The most distal HSA21q non-PCG and PCG, DSTNP1 (FPKM = 6.5) and PRMT2 (FPKM = 60.2), were detected as expressed.
source: The most proximal HSA21q non-PCG and PCG, ANKRD30BP2 (13,038,159–13,067,033, FPKM = 5.3) and POTED (13,038,159–13,067,033, FPKM = 2.4), respectively, were detected as expressed, as were the most distal HSA21q non-PCG and PCG, DSTNP1 (46,635,166–46,665,124, FPKM = 6.5) and PRMT2 (46,635,166–46,665,124, FPKM = 60.2) (Figure 2B).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2B

claim: Transcripts of HSA21 genes located in deleted regions were not detected.
source: Transcripts of HSA21 genes located in deleted regions were not detected.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data

claim: The HSA21q-MAC spans the whole long arm of HSA21.
source: These data further demonstrate that the HSA21q-MAC spans the whole long arm of HSA21, is consistent with deletion mapping from WGS, and indicates that the mouse chromosome background (MAC) does not interfere HSA21 gene transcription.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data showing expression of proximal and distal genes

claim: The mouse chromosome background (MAC) does not interfere with HSA21 gene transcription.
source: These data further demonstrate that the HSA21q-MAC spans the whole long arm of HSA21, is consistent with deletion mapping from WGS, and indicates that the mouse chromosome background (MAC) does not interfere HSA21 gene transcription.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data showing expression of HSA21 genes

claim: Most (476 of 487) HSA21 non-PCGs do not have a reported mouse ortholog.
source: Most (476 of 487) HSA21 non-PCGs do not have a reported mouse ortholog (Figure 2—source data 1A).
evidence: Based on annotation data shown in Figure 2—source data 1A

claim: Four HSA21 microRNAs have mouse orthologs, but transcript levels from either mouse or human microRNAs were extremely low or undetectable.
source: Four HSA21 microRNAs have mouse orthologs, but transcript levels from either mouse or human microRNAs were extremely low or undetectable (Figure 2—source data 1B).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2—source data 1B

claim: There are 160 PCGs on HSA21q (excluding KRTAPs) that have mouse orthologs.
source: There are 160 PCGs on HSA21q (excluding KRTAPs) that have mouse orthologs (Figure 2—source data 1C).
evidence: Based on annotation data shown in Figure 2—source data 1C

claim: 117 HSA21 mouse orthologs were expressed with FPKM ≥1 in Eu mice.
source: Of these, 117 HSA21 mouse orthologs were expressed with FPKM ≥1 in Eu mice (Figure 2C and Figure 2—source data 1D).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—source data 1D

claim: Expression of mouse orthologs was not substantially affected by the presence of HSA21q in TcMAC21, as 106 out of the 117 orthologs were expressed at 80–120% of Eu levels in TcMAC21.
source: Overall, expression of these mouse orthologs was not substantially affected by the presence of HSA21q in TcMAC21, as 106 out of the 117 orthologs were expressed at 80–120% of Eu levels in TcMAC21.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data comparing TcMAC21 and Eu

claim: Two mouse orthologs, Erg and Prdm15, had reduced expression (<0.8 fold) in TcMAC21.
source: Two mouse orthologs, Erg and Prdm15, had reduced expression (<0.8 fold), and nine mouse orthologs showed expression >1.2 fold in TcMAC21.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data comparing TcMAC21 and Eu

claim: Nine mouse orthologs showed expression >1.2 fold in TcMAC21.
source: Two mouse orthologs, Erg and Prdm15, had reduced expression (<0.8 fold), and nine mouse orthologs showed expression >1.2 fold in TcMAC21.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data comparing TcMAC21 and Eu

claim: Transcript levels of HSA21 PCGs were on average about half that of their mouse orthologs in Eu mice.
source: Transcript levels of HSA21 PCGs were on average about half that of their mouse orthologs in Eu mice as expected for a single copy of the human chromosome, but this HSA21/mouse ortholog expression ratio varied considerably among genes.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data comparing HSA21 and mouse ortholog expression

claim: Among intact HSA21 PCGs, 34.6% fell in the low overexpression range (<1.3 fold increased over Eu).
source: Among intact HSA21 PCGs, 34.6% fell in the low overexpression range (<1.3 fold increased over Eu), 29.9% were in the expected range (1.3–1.7-fold), 35.5% were highly overexpressed (>1.7 fold).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data analyzing total expression (HSA21 + mouse ortholog)

claim: Among intact HSA21 PCGs, 29.9% were in the expected range (1.3–1.7-fold).
source: Among intact HSA21 PCGs, 34.6% fell in the low overexpression range (<1.3 fold increased over Eu), 29.9% were in the expected range (1.3–1.7-fold), 35.5% were highly overexpressed (>1.7 fold).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data analyzing total expression (HSA21 + mouse ortholog)

claim: Among intact HSA21 PCGs, 35.5% were highly overexpressed (>1.7 fold).
source: Among intact HSA21 PCGs, 34.6% fell in the low overexpression range (<1.3 fold increased over Eu), 29.9% were in the expected range (1.3–1.7-fold), 35.5% were highly overexpressed (>1.7 fold).
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data analyzing total expression (HSA21 + mouse ortholog)

claim: 712 mouse genes in TcMAC21 were down-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu <0.8) among 13976 mouse genes whose FPKM ≥ 1 in Eu.
source: We found 712 of these genes in TcMAC21 were down-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu <0.8) and 1191 genes were up-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu >1.2), indicating that, as in other mouse models and people with trisomy 21, steady state RNA levels are perturbed throughout the genome.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data analyzing genome-wide gene expression

claim: 1191 mouse genes in TcMAC21 were up-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu >1.2) among 13976 mouse genes whose FPKM ≥ 1 in Eu.
source: We found 712 of these genes in TcMAC21 were down-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu <0.8) and 1191 genes were up-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu >1.2), indicating that, as in other mouse models and people with trisomy 21, steady state RNA levels are perturbed throughout the genome.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq data analyzing genome-wide gene expression

claim: In other mouse models and people with trisomy 21, steady state RNA levels are perturbed throughout the genome.
source: We found 712 of these genes in TcMAC21 were down-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu <0.8) and 1191 genes were up-regulated (TcMAC21/Eu >1.2), indicating that, as in other mouse models and people with trisomy 21, steady state RNA levels are perturbed throughout the genome.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about trisomy 21 effects

claim: Relative expression quantified by Taqman RT-PCR was significantly correlated with that determined by RNA-Seq (R = 0.96, p<0.0001).
source: Relative expression quantified by Taqman RT-PCR was significantly correlated with that determined by RNA-Seq (R = 0.96, p<0.0001) (Figure 2D).
evidence: Based on Taqman RT-PCR validation data shown in Figure 2D

claim: HSA21 PCG expression levels in forebrain and hindbrain were very similar and frequently different from levels of the same transcript in heart.
source: Taqman RT-PCR of different tissues of P1 TcMAC21 mice showed that HSA21 PCG expression levels in forebrain and hindbrain were very similar and frequently different from levels of the same transcript in heart, consistent with tissue-specific regulation of HSA21 genes (Figure 2E).
evidence: Based on Taqman RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2E

claim: HSA21 genes are subject to tissue-specific regulation.
source: Taqman RT-PCR of different tissues of P1 TcMAC21 mice showed that HSA21 PCG expression levels in forebrain and hindbrain were very similar and frequently different from levels of the same transcript in heart, consistent with tissue-specific regulation of HSA21 genes (Figure 2E).
evidence: Based on Taqman RT-PCR data showing tissue-specific expression patterns

claim: HSA21q is actively transcribed and regulated to produce dosage imbalance in TcMAC21.
source: Thus, these results indicate that HSA21q is actively transcribed and regulated to produce dosage imbalance in TcMAC21.
evidence: Based on RNA-Seq and RT-PCR data showing expression and regulation of HSA21 genes

claim: GFP appears to be a reliable marker for genotyping TcMAC21.
source: Including the TcMAC21 mouse used for WGS, we saw 100% concordance of GFP with HSA21q gene expression across the chromosome and zero false positives among fifteen pairs. Thus, GFP appears to be a reliable marker for genotyping TcMAC21.
evidence: Based on validation data showing 100% concordance between GFP and HSA21q gene expression

claim: The HSA21q-MAC was detected in ≥96% of TcMAC21 cells in several dissociated tissues analyzed by FISH.
source: Several tissues were dissociated and analyzed using FISH, whereby the HSA21q-MAC was detected in ≥96% of TcMAC21 cells (Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Based on FISH data shown in Figure 3C–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C

claim: Flow cytometry (FCM) analysis of lymphocytes showed that over 92% of TcMAC21 cells were GFP positive.
source: Similarly, flow cytometry (FCM) analysis of lymphocytes showed that over 92% of TcMAC21 cells were GFP positive (Figure 3E).
evidence: Based on FCM data shown in Figure 3E

claim: All Purkinje cells (PCs) in TcMAC21 were GFP positive while those in Eu were GFP negative.
source: Immunostaining of parasagittal brain sections with calbindin antibody showed all Purkinje cells (PCs) in TcMAC21 were GFP positive while those in Eu were GFP negative (Figure 3F).
evidence: Based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 3F

claim: If mosaicism occurs at all in TcMAC21, it is rare.
source: Together, these findings indicate that, if it occurs at all, mosaicism is rare in TcMAC21.
evidence: Based on FISH, FCM, and immunostaining data showing high retention rates

claim: CHDs are present in nearly half of newborns with DS.
source: CHDs are present in nearly half of newborns with DS and include septal defects, such as the complete AV canal form of atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), and atrial septal defect (ASD), plus outflow tract abnormalities, such as double outlet right ventricle (DORV).
evidence: Based on established clinical knowledge about DS

claim: Several mouse DS models show high rates of CHD.
source: Several mouse DS models show high rates of CHD, as well (Williams et al., 2008; Lana-Elola et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Williams et al., 2008; Lana-Elola et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012

claim: 28.6% of TcMAC21 had a structural defect of the heart.
source: We found that 28.6% of TcMAC21 had a structural defect of the heart by consolidating data of both assays (Figure 4C).
evidence: Based on wet dissection and histology data shown in Figure 4C

claim: VSD was the predominant malformation in TcMAC21, accounting for 21.4%.
source: VSD was the predominant malformation, accounting for 21.4%, and AVSD accounting for 2.4%.
evidence: Based on wet dissection and histology data

claim: AVSD in TcMAC21 accounted for 2.4%.
source: VSD was the predominant malformation, accounting for 21.4%, and AVSD accounting for 2.4%.
evidence: Based on wet dissection and histology data

claim: The 24% frequency of septal defects in TcMAC21 is substantially greater than the 4% observed in Ts65Dn mice but smaller than the 38–55% reported in Tc1.
source: The 24% frequency of septal defects in TcMAC21 is substantially greater than the 4% observed in Ts65Dn mice but smaller than the 38–55% reported in Tc1 (O'Doherty et al., 2005; Williams et al., 2008; Li et al., 2012; Dunlevy et al., 2010).
evidence: Based on comparison with published data from other DS mouse models, supported by citations

claim: AVSD occurs in 20% of newborns with DS but is rare or absent from DS mouse models except in the presence of additional genetic modifiers.
source: AVSD occurs in 20% of newborns with DS but is rare or absent from DS mouse models except in the presence of additional genetic modifiers (Li et al., 2012; Polk et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Li et al., 2012 and Polk et al., 2015

claim: Cerebellar hypoplasia is among the few phenotypes present in every person with DS.
source: Cerebellar hypoplasia is among the few phenotypes present in every person with DS (Aylward et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Aylward et al., 1997

claim: Analysis of Ts65Dn identified a deficit in cerebellar granule cells and correctly predicted its occurrence in people with DS.
source: Analysis of Ts65Dn identified a deficit in cerebellar granule cells and correctly predicted its occurrence in people with DS (Baxter et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baxter et al., 2000

claim: Cerebellar granule cell deficit is present in several DS mouse models.
source: This deficit is present in several DS mouse models as well (Olson et al., 2004; Dutka et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Olson et al., 2004 and Dutka et al., 2015

claim: Ventricle enlargement is associated with neurodegenerative diseases and aneuploidies including DS.
